fullDaySay: You push through the doors into open air. Haven grounds — tents, a fire pit, worn paths. The world is that way.
You break ground behind the hall — bed 1 of 2, turned and ready. Sow seed to start a crop.
You break ground behind the hall — bed 2 of 2, turned and ready. Sow seed to start a crop.
💧 A woman, maybe 60s, with a buzz cut returns with water: +3 clean.
🚶 A woman, maybe 50s is back — found A person, maybe 50s.
📨 Word came: Onni Korhonen wants to join Haven. "Word travels: Haven takes people in. I'm people." — they haven't set foot here. The village will judge.
📓 Journal: Onni Korhonen applied remotely.

"Hey." A person, maybe 30s, with restless hands settles near you, not too close. "Day one. Everyone's pretending they're fine. ...Can we talk? Just talk — like people used to." (Talk to A person, maybe 30s, with restless hands.)
Recipe: Bark armor (Level 1). You have seen bark armor. Plates of bark laced together, worn like a shell.

🛡️ Dawn at Haven. By the fire hangs an old bark cuirass, split at the seam — somebody's grandfather wore this into the treeline and came back. The shape of it is clear: bark plates laced overlapping like shingles, vine cord. Your hands don't know it yet. Your eyes do.
⚠ STARVING: health and energy falling. You went to bed on an empty stomach.
Village meal: +1200 kcal, +1L water from the communal pantry. (Half ration — they don't trust you yet.)
A man, maybe 60s is staring into the fire like it owes them answers.
A person, maybe 50s traded something with someone for something else. The barter economy stirs.
Jacob and Vincent lingered over the fire together.
Giulia and Jacob lingered over the fire together.
Boris and Vincent lingered over the fire together.
Zoe and Jacob lingered over the fire together.

🤒 Jacob is achy and wrung out, barely eating. Rest and clean water — or it gets worse.
— DAY 2 DAWN — The world wakes. Animals are active.

🔥 Werner has been turning something over all evening. Finally: “Boris. The past story — we all eat from the same pot here, we don’t get to lie about who’s at it.” It costs Werner to say it; you can see the price land.

Boris is quiet for a long moment. Then, all in a rush: “Fine. It’s true. Not Denver — Kraków, Poland. I lied because the truth felt small.” The admission hangs there, and the village — to its credit — doesn’t pounce.
People bring you their suspicions, written down. You keep every one.
A person, maybe 30s, with restless hands will work the garden once each day while at Haven. Other orders take priority.
You step into the Haven hall.
A person, maybe 50s looks at you flatly. "Why should I listen to you?" (Trust too low.)
📋 A person, maybe 30s, with restless hands — 🎣 Fish. They'll report back by next part.
A person, maybe 50s shakes their head. "Ask someone who trusts you." (Trust too low.)
📋 A man, maybe 30s — 🎣 Fish. They'll report back by next part.
A person, maybe 50s doesn't say a word. They just stand there, arms crossed, until you finish giving the order. The silence does the talking.
(Talking costs a little energy — 10 kcal a conversation. Small talk is cheap; going deep costs time, not more food.)
Hunger gnaws. The pack is thin — work the green, haul it back, get it named at camp. That's the whole game.
"Asher," they say, touching their chest. "I'm Asher." You'll remember that.
📓 Journal: learned their name (Asher).
"Desmond," they say, touching their chest. "I'm Desmond." You'll remember that.
📓 Journal: learned their name (Desmond).
...and then it lands: A man, maybe 60s speaks 🇵🇱 Polish. You share no language at all.
They point at themself and say it slowly, twice. It sounds like a name: Boris.
📓 Journal: learned their name (Boris).
Boris speaks only 🇵🇱 Polish. No shared words at all — just eyes, hands, and patience.

Travel 1 tile to meadow.
— Open ground —
Grasshoppers rise in a clicking wave ahead of you. Something fork-tailed rides the wind above them, waiting for the careless ones.
Something big is moving in the woods. The birds went quiet.
You catch fragments by the fire — Asher telling Desmond about Vincent. It's barely the same story now. That's what fires do.

You catch fragments by the fire — A person, maybe 30s, with sun-creased eyes telling A woman, maybe 60s, with grey-streaked hair about Vincent. The truth left this story two fires ago. What's left is better theater.
This patch is worked out — step to another green patch and forage again.

Travel 2 tiles to creek.
— Moving water —
The water is cold enough to hurt your teeth. Downstream the creek bends out of sight, and you want to follow it. That's the problem with creeks.
✅ You saw the creek. Boris nods. "Good. Now we know." (+integration)
This patch is worked out — step to another green patch and forage again.
The creek runs fast here — no crossing without a bridge or a swim.

📓 Journal: the woman in her 60s, with grey-streaked hair taught the woman in her 20s Old World Caches.

🛟 Vincent stands up by the fire. "People are going down and the tents are filling — we do something or we don't, but we decide. Here's what we CAN do — pick one, maybe two, but everything costs something."
"The sick need tending — triage tents, broth, boiled water. Or we tighten our belts and wait it out. Or the hale hunt while the sick lie still."
"Or we rally," Vincent adds. "Second shift, everybody. We work, we eat, we live — and we pay for it."
(Relief is open — triage, rations, hunt, or rally, from the beats row. Each option works once; the moment passes in ~3 days.)
📓 Journal: Vincent proposed relief (sickness), day 3.
